reviews.text: My name is Sònia and I have 5 children, two biological, Ferran and Marina and three adopted, Popa, Proa and Tuna. Popa was adopted when she was two years old from a shelter in La Garrotxa, she is now 15. On Sunday, October 4, 2026, they saw her very apathetic, with a hard belly and retching without vomiting, we were scared and took her to the emergency room at the Monjuïc veterinary hospital. The diagnosis was devastating, stomach torsion and two options, euthanasia or an emergency operation with a lot of risk given that she is a very large dog. The cries of me and my children will remember her for a while at the center ☺️. They decided to operate and at 2:30 in the morning, surgeon Ignacio Montes de Oca called me, with a kindness and empathy that I will never forget, to give me the best news, everything had gone well and Popa was already waking up. Sometimes people you have never met become the heroes of a family. Popa was admitted for three days and they were able to visit her. I have no words to thank the humane treatment received, the love with which they treated my daughter and the kindness of all the staff. A special thank you to surgeon Ignacio Montes de Oca who saved her life and to his wife, also a surgeon at the center who gave us the control visit. I will always take you to ♥️

Excellent professionals. We went there for an emergency, referred from another veterinary hospital with a very serious prognosis, and they attended to us incredibly quickly.

The care we received was exceptional, and thanks to them, our dog Ringo is recovering very well. We are grateful for the dedication and compassion of the entire team, especially our veterinary neurologist, Anna García, who kept us informed every step of the way and comforted and encouraged us after a few hours of despair.

I highly recommend this Veterinary Hospital for urgent cases, as they are open 24 hours a day and act as quickly as necessary in every situation.

And I'll say it again, thank you so much for your excellent service at every moment, from the first to the last. 💖🐕

I have no words to express my gratitude for the work of the professionals at the Veterinary Hospital. Their kindness, patience, and compassion extend not only to the pets but also to the humans who accompany them.

Despite the time, effort, and expense invested in Niko, it wasn't meant to be. 🥺 But I am incredibly grateful for the kind and compassionate care I received from the professionals: María, Lidia, Silvia, Roger, and others.

It was months of consultations, emergency room visits, hospitalizations, tests, and above all, desperation to find out what was wrong with him and what could be done for him. Unfortunately, even with the diagnosis and treatment in place, nothing more could be done for my little boy. I would have continued and done everything possible for him, but at the last minute, everything became complicated, and his organs began to fail. So, after making a very painful decision, we put him to sleep because it was time. I also want to thank Roger Llauradó for the gentle farewell and the kindness he showed, and for allowing me to have my time and hold my baby in my arms until his last heartbeat.

Thanks to Silvia for her incredible empathy and the love she showed me when she heard the bad news, and thanks to María García for being so attentive to Niko and taking the time to write to me when she found out.

🫂❤️😻 The professionals were fantastic, but the prices, while I understand it's a hospital and not a neighborhood clinic with specialists and the necessary equipment, are exorbitant, especially when dozens of tests are required. I've had to scrape together the money, but what if you don't have it? Financing isn't an option either, because if you don't have it, you can't pay, and when you love them so much and they're like family, the desperation is even greater. They were kind enough to give me a small discount on some bills, but it's still thousands of euros.
Perfect.
Rafa, thank you so much for your kindness during such a difficult time. An incredible team. India will be eternally grateful 🖤🐕‍🦺 …

Hello! I've been calling several times and I keep getting an answering machine. I don't think you're providing good customer service. You're leaving customers on hold with an answering machine and not answering.
I don't think it's right for a hospital to have such terrible service.

Hello:

Thank you so much for your feedback and for the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!

A surreal experience: I called to ask about the neurologist's schedule, was put on hold, and the inept receptionist didn't mute the call, so I overheard the entire conversation: "She thinks we're going to pull a fast one on her," "Then I'll tell her to come whenever she damn well pleases." UNACCEPTABLE! I expect management to address this.

I find the lack of empathy and sensitivity shown towards someone concerned about their pet's health and trying to find specialized care based on their veterinarian's recommendation particularly troubling.

Furthermore, the fact that these comments were made under the mistaken belief that I couldn't hear them is especially concerning from a customer service perspective and regarding the professionalism expected of the staff at your center.

The truth is, my experience was excellent. From the very first moment, Ángela at reception answered the phone with incredible empathy and sensitivity, and her tone of voice was so appreciated in such a stressful situation. She was very kind and treated me with genuine compassion.

Later, Roger, one of the veterinarians, was a tremendous help in deciding what to do, how to proceed, and what my options were, always looking for the best solution for Jinx.

It was a weekend emergency, and I was quite worried, but Roger treated my cat incredibly well, with great care and explaining everything clearly. The service was outstanding.

I am so grateful for both the care I received and the way they supported us during such a difficult time. Without a doubt, it was a very positive experience, despite how challenging it is to have to take your pet to the emergency room.

Hi Patricia,

Thank you so much for your feedback and for trusting our team.

Best regards!

The convenient parking. The professional veterinary team. I warned that my dog ​​could not stand up and that she was screaming and in a lot of pain. She had to stand for 2 hours when I explicitly said that she could not wait for her to stand up because it aggravates her condition. I will not return. I prefer to pay more but that they prioritize the well-being of all the animals, since when it comes to charging everything goes very quickly. We are talking about living beings, not objects

My dog ​​was admitted to this clinic for a herniated disc. Upon her discharge, we were told she needed to remain on complete rest for several weeks. We later had a follow-up appointment with a very kind veterinarian who explained that we should call back in about two weeks to discuss the next steps.
Those two weeks have passed, and we've spent the last two days trying to contact the clinic. They often don't answer the phone, and when we finally get through, they tell us they can't see us at that moment.

I can completely understand that there might be emergencies or that the staff is busy, but I find it totally unacceptable that in two days they haven't been able to find even a few minutes to contact us. We're talking about our dog's health, and to this day, we don't know how to proceed with her recovery. Meanwhile, she remains in a cage, following the prescribed rest, and we are completely lost about what to do next.

The lack of communication and follow-up in a situation like this seems very unprofessional and, frankly, quite disappointing. We're not asking for immediate or priority attention, just basic communication to know how to proceed with our dog's treatment.

I'm writing this review hoping that, at least through this channel, someone will contact us and explain how we should continue.
Zeus was saved at the last moment, thank you for everything you have done.

I took my dog ​​there and they admitted him, but they didn't do anything at all (not even an IV), yet they still charged me an exorbitant amount. The worst part is that after two weeks they haven't even asked about my dog, nor have they sent me the test results or the vet report. I have to keep demanding them as if I hadn't paid. While he was admitted, I went to visit him and suspiciously they made me wait half an hour, and the same thing happened when I went to pick him up after his discharge. What condition was the dog in that I had to wait so long to see him? I would never recommend you. You have zero love for animals, let alone respect for people.
Everything's fine except the price, but not at this particular hospital. Everything's just becoming prohibitively expensive.

As a veterinary service, it's good. The dog has been very well cared for. As for humanitarian service, I'm sorry but I have to say that for me it's disastrous.
We had an appointment to visit and give the dog results on 09/16, the day we were on alert due to rain and for logistical reasons, and having warned them and since they have paid for everything, they let us visit after a week, without caring about our suffering to know the results and just looking at how the wound is.
A little call at least to say the results, I don't find it so excessive, but of course they have already paid and it seems that they are taking advantage of what we love about our pets.

Hi Maria,

Thank you so much for your feedback and for trusting our team.

Best regards!
Excellent, the best I've ever been to.

The best experience during one of the toughest times of my life. They are extremely professional and rigorous in their quality of care, but without neglecting the human aspect.
Federico (a bulldog) had a cervical hernia and was in a lot of pain. I arrived at the emergency room and they treated him with great professionalism and care from the very first moment. A week later he was discharged and back home as if nothing had happened. Every morning, Dr. Ana G. from neurology called me to give me an update on how he had done the night and his progress. The level of follow-up, care, concern, and attention made all the difference during such a worrying time.
I am deeply grateful to the entire team who were part of this, especially Dr. Ana for her professionalism, Hugo and Mar from nursing, and Aida from reception. Each of you made a difference in my life and Federico's. Hugo, thank you for giving Federico a kiss every time you took him out of his cage. Thanks to you, I felt much more at ease knowing Federico was sleeping somewhere other than our house. Thank you, Ana, for every call and for giving me peace of mind knowing Federico was in the best hands. Thank you, Aida, for greeting me with a smile at reception.

Thank you, Mar, for raising my concerns with the veterinary team whenever I was nervous.

Thank you all so much ♥️
Now Federico is walking again without pain and has regained his energy. He has six weeks of rest ahead, but I am completely at ease thanks to you all. And although it was a difficult time, if I had to go through something like this again, I would think of you first thing without hesitation.
♥️🫶🏻✨🤍🥰🐶🙏🏻

I went to the emergency service on August 19, 2026, at 5:00 AM. I am not a veterinarian, and I have no doubt about the professionals at this center. My experience with the person who attended to me was very negative. As a professional, she would know that I could describe what was happening to my dog, who was unable to sleep day and night, minute after minute. Neither my dog ​​nor I could sleep because of the symptoms of not being able to rest, and I was obviously trying to help her. That's why we went to the emergency room when what I thought was a bad cold was getting worse, preventing her from breathing through her nostrils. She had also lost her sense of smell and appetite. I also noticed a lump on her neck, which I thought was lymphatic, like what happens in people to fight infections or viruses. I repeat, I am not a veterinarian. I told the doctor that her airways had been blocked for days, though not as blocked as that night. Unfortunately, our veterinarian was on vacation, and that's why we came here, since I had heard very good things about it. I doubt the help that other families have received. I explained that my dog ​​would try to sleep, and after a few seconds, no air would get through her nostrils, and she would wake up agitated and panting, repeating this cycle. Clearly, there was a significant infection and a lot of mucus. She told me she didn't see any mucus. Perplexed, I told her that's why she couldn't breathe. She said to do a chest x-ray, I think, not an ultrasound, and that her chest, lungs, and heart looked fine. But because she's a very fearful and restless dog, they couldn't handle a 15-kilo dog. I don't think they did the important one, the abdominal x-ray, which would have been an ultrasound, because I understand that's where they would have seen the tumorous masses that were detected days later in an ultrasound at another center. I'm not a veterinarian, and this is just my opinion. As a doctor, you can't excuse yourself by saying you can't handle a 15-kilo dog and your assistants. You tell me that, and I'll go down and... I'm helping you because she needs to know from her experience that this isn't a simple cold and could be something much more serious. She looked at a recent blood test with a liver value of approximately 382, ​​which is high, but we had been giving her liver medication with our vet for a long time to regulate it. I think that as a professional, with this clinical picture of liver function and what I already explained to her, she should have acted urgently and done that ultrasound to quickly rule out tumors. Her treatment was an antibiotic and sent home. I'm not a veterinarian, and I thought that would help clear the mucus and the cold I thought she had, and everything would be fine. Oh, 10 minutes of explaining and examining my dog, and 300 euros, and sent home. It's not the money anymore, it's the lack of management and professionalism. I'm not including your registration number because I'm not cruel. What I do find cruel is that after a few days, because we trusted that diagnosis, we admitted her to another center, they did an ultrasound and biopsies on the tumors, and my dog ​​died of cancer. Lymphoma on August 30, 2026. We would have gained so much time if they had been more professional here in Mexico and had taken our visit to the center more seriously, instead of putting my dog ​​and my family through this agony. The outcome, unfortunately, might have been the same, but we would have gained days for chemotherapy and cortisone treatment with a stronger body and stomach. The poor thing was vomiting everything with the feeding tube. They boast about your professionalism and attention on their website, but what you deserve is a serious complaint. To all owners: don't let them fool you with stories. If you see a serious problem, demand an ultrasound, and if the dog is stable enough, a CT scan. Unlike me, who visited other veterinarians before and after Anicura and after Mexico, and all they know how to do is take your money and not get to the point. As the days go by, our beloved pets weaken, and there are no treatments left to save them.

I have no words to express my gratitude for the care my dog, Mia, received in the emergency room yesterday.

From the incredibly kind and helpful receptionist, to the orthopedic surgeon who saw me immediately, and to Rafa. Thank you for your warmth and transparency, your tact and clarity from the very first moment.
Mia was in good hands, and we are so grateful.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We've been with them for over 13 years and we couldn't be happier. Nina is undergoing treatment and we're sure that, with the love and care she's receiving, she'll pull through. ❤️🐶

Golfo and our little Corgi Queen are also in the best hands. Special thanks to Sílvia Tremosa, Marta Seguí, Irene Moñiz, Lluís, and the entire team for their effort, dedication, and commitment to our furry friends. 🐾❤️
Very good service, especially in Oncology.

A 10 out of 10 for the entire team at the Montjuïc Veterinary Hospital. They are highly professional, clear, honest, and above all, incredibly kind and caring.

I've been taking my dog ​​Dina there for years, and she's always received excellent care. They've consistently been spot on, diagnosing complex illnesses and providing highly effective treatments.

Currently, I want to especially highlight the work of Lluís Benítez, Dina's oncologist. He's fantastic, a true professional, and also approachable and clear in his explanations.

I am so, so grateful!! 😍

Hi Claudia,

Thank you so much for your feedback and for trusting our team.

Best regards!
We want to express our gratitude for the outstanding professionalism shown by every member of this hospital staff over the past 18 years! Thank you for everything!
Exceptional service. Cancer treatment for a female dog.

Hi Regina,

Thank you so much for your feedback and for trusting our team.

Hugs!

An excellent experience at this veterinary hospital. From the very first moment, they treated our pet with great professionalism, warmth, and care.

I especially want to highlight Óscar for his kindness, dedication, and the calming presence he exudes. It's clear he's a true professional who genuinely cares about the animals' well-being. He explained everything clearly and was attentive throughout our visit.

Without a doubt, this veterinary hospital is highly recommended, and I especially want to thank Óscar for the wonderful care we received. Thank you so much for everything!

I've been taking my animals there my whole life, especially for emergencies and other sad situations.

Except for a terrible experience two years ago during a euthanasia.
Everything else has always been excellent.
Three days ago, my Peppa was admitted, and I couldn't be happier with the treatment I received from all the staff. Excellent medical team, assistants, and reception staff.

We went to this hospital because of a life-threatening emergency involving our cat, but we are very dissatisfied with the treatment we received. We didn't like the attitude of most of the veterinarians we saw at all, including the specialist who only seemed to care about us accepting the exorbitant estimate instead of providing clear explanations, and she showed absolutely no empathy. We also don't understand why a hospital like this doesn't have anyone available to perform ultrasounds on weekends...

After wasting a lot of time with a completely incorrect diagnosis, they didn't know how to handle the case, and the veterinarian called us with a coldness we've never seen before, telling us that we had to tell her if we really wanted to continue treatment or if we wanted euthanasia, even without having clear information about the situation. A situation like this requires much more empathy and asking the owners in person to discuss options!

The coldness with which patients and their owners are treated is shameful; it shows a complete lack of professionalism! If you love your pet, don't bring them here. There are much better places where they'll receive better care.
Fortunately, our cat took her last breath at another center, surrounded by wonderful professionals with huge hearts who did everything they could for her.

A year ago, we arrived at this hospital heartbroken. We had come from another center where they told us our dog, Leo, had very little chance of survival. Then you came into our lives, especially the oncologist Luis and the entire team at Montjuïc Hospital. You gave us hope when we had almost lost it. You continued his treatment and supported us with extraordinary professionalism and compassion. Today, a year later, Leo is still with us, fighting. And we are enjoying every day by his side, something we thought we would never experience again. There are no words to express our gratitude to Luis and the entire team. Thank you for your commitment, your love for animals, and for not giving up when others had already lost hope. You will always hold a very special place in our hearts. Thank you for giving him and our family this opportunity to live.

Hi Mari,

Thank you so much for your feedback.

We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!

Hello, José Antonio:

Thank you so much for your feedback.

We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!
Good, accompanied

Hi Aida,

We're so glad to receive your feedback.

Thank you so much for your trust!

Hugs.
Everything perfect
A team of professionals and they treated my dog ​​very well. Thank you so much 🙏🏻 🤍 …

Words can't express my gratitude, because all I can say is THANK YOU to the entire team at Hospital Veterinai Montjuic, especially Ana Garcia (Neurologist). From the very first moment, she was lovely, clear, and strict about the rest period.
She gave us hope that everything could turn out alright, even with the possibility of things going wrong… We decided to go ahead, and they saved our 14-year-old Nay.
She had surgery for a herniated disc that had compressed her spinal cord.
Nay was listless, had a urinary tract infection, hadn't wagged her tail for months, wasn't eating, her gaze was vacant, and she could barely walk… She was hospitalized and cared for with all the love in the world. They made sure we knew it when we were finally able to visit her.
And now I look at her, and she has recovered that beautiful gaze she has, her will to live, and she is pain-free. Our veterinarian, Trivet (Calafell), recommended this hospital to us, and we will be eternally grateful.
Thank you from the bottom of our hearts to everyone, but I must mention Ana again; she was our angel.

Disastrous experience with the Montjuïc Veterinary Hospital. My dog ​​died after being treated at this veterinary hospital.

I took my dog ​​there and, after her death in March 2024, I have repeatedly requested all of her medical documentation, from the day of her death: results of ultrasounds, biopsies, lab tests, medication and other tests performed. However, they only provided me with an incomplete clinical report and, despite my repeated requests, I have not received all the information requested.

I believe that my dog ​​died as a result of the actions of this center. I am particularly concerned that she was given anesthesia to perform an ultrasound that, as I had expressly indicated over the phone, she did not want to have, and yet when I arrived they had already done it. After what happened, I am convinced that this action had fatal consequences for her.

Since the day of her death I have tried to obtain all the necessary information to know exactly what was done to her, what medication was administered and what happened during the procedure. However, after more than two years of requests, I still do not have all the medical documentation.

This lack of transparency and explanations has only increased my doubts and distrust. If everything that was done was justified and acted correctly, I do not understand why it has been impossible to obtain complete documentation for my own dog.

The lack of transparency, communication and respect that I have experienced has been totally disappointing. On the other hand, when it came to collecting the money, the management was fast.

I do not recommend this center. When you leave your animal's life in the hands of a veterinary team, you expect professionalism, transparency and trust. Unfortunately, I lost my dog ​​and to this day I have not received all the explanations and documentation that I requested.

I want to express my heartfelt gratitude to **Lluís Benítez, oncologist**, and **Lola Torres, ophthalmologist**, for the excellent treatment and care they provided to **Railway, our beloved dog**.

The diagnosis and treatment of her mast cell tumor were a huge worry for us, but thanks to their professionalism, experience, and dedication, everything went wonderfully. **The surgery was excellent, the mast cell tumor has been completely eradicated, and the eyelid reconstruction was magnificent.**

We couldn't be more grateful for their work and the loving care they showed Railway throughout the entire process.

**Thank you so much, Lluís and Lola, for restoring our peace of mind and for taking such good care of our little one.** ❤️🐾

I would like to express my gratitude for the care I received during a critical situation. The treatment was both humane and professional, with special thanks to Silvia the veterinarian, although the entire team was very kind.

I have no words to thank you for everything you did for our little Lottus. From the very first moment, you made us feel supported, explained everything to us with so much patience, and above all, treated him with a love and dedication we will never forget.

In the most difficult moments, knowing he was in the hands of such a professional and caring team gave us so much peace of mind. Thank you for taking care of Lottus as if he were your own and for giving us back hope.

And a special thanks to Ana, Silvia, and Lluis.

You are an incredible team. We will always be grateful to you. You are the best! ❤️🐾
The service is very, very good, the attention they provide is excellent! Dr. Ana is very good and kind.

Hi Nicole,

Thank you so much for your feedback.

We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Hugs!

I wish someone had warned me NOT to come here. In short: the IV pole was always on the floor, and that's where they administer medication directly into the vein. It gets infected because of the dirt on the floor. I warned them a couple of times on different visits; they would put it in, but it would come out again through the opening in the IV chamber. And from a blood infection, the patient dies. They call you to decide whether to euthanize them. They tell you the patient is critical and that you have 10 minutes to decide, and by then they've arrived at the ER. I left them well after the transfusion. It's a factory-like place where different people work each shift; you never see the same people. Even the people on the previous morning shift weren't the same as those on the next. In the afternoon, the same thing happened all five times we were seen, and different people were there. There's no follow-up for one or two patients. The afternoon shift guy couldn't find my cat's chart to check and record new values. He spent 10 minutes looking for it before he finally found it. I would NEVER have taken him there if I had known what it's like...at least for those of us who aren't regular customers.

FULL STORY: We went there because our vet told us he needed an urgent transfusion, as his hematocrit was at 11 and we had to take him to a hospital that had blood. My daughter called several hospitals, and they all said we had to request it from the blood bank. BUT HERE THEY TOLD HER THEY HAD BLOOD, WHICH WAS A LIE. THEY TRICKED US to charge us. We went to the EMERGENCY at 7 PM without hesitation. We sent all the tests done by my vet that same day and an ultrasound from two days prior. Even so, they repeated the tests (we found out the next day). They had previously given us a quote that covered the cost of the blood, so they could administer it urgently. Under the pretext of determining his blood type (A or B), they drew blood again, and that was on the same day, with such a small amount. He was admitted. At the shift change, a kind young veterinarian attended to us and told us there was blood available in Terrassa, and I told her to give it to him immediately. She said that if necessary, they would bring it urgently (it was already urgent, but apparently they don't do that at night). The next day, I went to visit and saw that they still hadn't given him the transfusion. He's on IV fluids, with a low dose so his blood doesn't get diluted. They should have given it subcutaneously, which takes longer to absorb, instead of directly into a vein.
I see he's more lethargic. I insist they didn't give him the transfusion; they said they always stabilize him first... he arrived stabilized from my vet.
They said there was blood in Granollers that they were going to bring it urgently, and it was 5 pm and it still hadn't arrived. I saw him gagging, and my daughter and I were crying. I said he was suffering, we should euthanize him if it didn't arrive. Then a guy said the blood had arrived, and we decided to give it to him. Alba gave it to him; she was the only one I saw with more compassion. She informed us, let us see him halfway through (it takes more than 3 hours), and let us see him at the end, almost asleep. He recovered; he was getting up and interacting. We went to sleep happy. The next morning he was lethargic again. My daughter tried to feed him boiled chicken and tuna, but he wouldn't eat. He went two days and two nights without drinking. I realized this because at 4 pm I arrived with a can of unsalted natural tuna. He still wouldn't eat. I asked for a water bowl (which I hadn't seen him have for two days) and he started drinking like crazy. He usually drank very little, never so much all at once. I know my cat well, he's almost 17 years old, and he's never drunk like that. I gave him tuna crumbs directly, and he ate them. Then he still wouldn't drink, so I asked for a syringe and gave him four 3 or 4 ml syringes. Then visiting hours were over. They told me I had to leave because the shift change was at 9 pm, and I left feeling relieved because, finally, after two days of not having food or water, he had drunk from me. The IV pole was still rolling on the floor (I warned him when I arrived and saw it; it was like that every time I came to visit. IT'S SERIOUS and it made things worse). Twenty minutes later I was on the train. They called to say he'd worsened a lot and to come quickly. I arrived. And he was no longer in the oxygen-heat chamber, but on oxygen to his face in the operating room. He's still there, then there's no more room. 👁️photos

We've been seeing them for over a year now for Rotti's cancer and chronic illnesses, and I couldn't be more grateful. Especially to Lluís and María G. Thank you so much for everything you've done and continue to do for Rotti. You're our go-to vets, even though we live far away, and we always recommend you to everyone ❤️🙏🏻 …

We want to thank the Montjuïc Veterinary Hospital, especially Diego and the entire Traumatology team, as well as the nurses and reception staff, for their professionalism, kindness, and the wonderful care we received.

Our dog Duke's cruciate ligament surgery went very well. They've already removed the bandage, and the latest x-ray shows the tear has healed beautifully, so we're very happy with his progress.

Now it's our turn to do the hardest part: keeping him from jumping or running and always taking him out on a leash. He's so eager to go back to playing with his friends at the dog park and gets angry when we don't let him! 😅🤣

Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your professionalism, attention, and care throughout the entire process. We wholeheartedly recommend this hospital. 🐾❤️

Hi Cristina,

Thank you so much for your feedback.

We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!

Hi Leo,

Thank you so much for your feedback.

We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!

I am so grateful to the incredibly professional and caring team at HV Montjuïc. My dog ​​has had two surgeries and several hospitalizations here this year for various reasons, and I always feel confident that she's in the best hands. The facilities are spotless, the service is excellent, and the fact that they're available 24/7 is a huge relief in emergencies. Thank you all from Kahlo 🫶🏼

I had high expectations for this hospital, but I didn't expect the administration and the work here to be so chaotic.

I fed my puppy canned and homemade food as advised by the vet. The homemade food made things worse. The canned food was gone, my puppy was very hungry and a little dehydrated, so I rushed to this hospital from Badalona at midnight.

I checked with the hospital before coming, and they made it clear they could sell me the food; I just needed to wait a little while.

I waited half an hour after arriving, they told me I had to wait, and after another half hour, they told me I would have to wait until all the emergencies were finished. The man who answered my phone said my situation wasn't urgent, so I needed to keep waiting.

I understand that my situation isn't as serious compared to the dying dogs, but my puppy is only two months old, and a long fast will have a huge impact on her stomach.

And the main thing is that I could have been clearly informed in the previous call so I could decide if it was worth coming at midnight (since it was a long drive from Badalona).
But the man didn't tell me anything.

I deeply regret his lack of consideration and irresponsibility.

Hi Javier,

Thank you so much for your feedback. We sincerely appreciate the trust you've placed in our team.

Best regards!

Yesterday I took my dog ​​Lleiko to the Montjuïc Veterinary Hospital for a neurology appointment, and the experience was excellent. Rafa and his colleagues saw us, and I want to highlight their friendliness, humility, and professionalism. It's clear he's passionate about his work, and the way he explains things is very reassuring and inspires confidence. It's wonderful to find professionals like this, so dedicated and compassionate, especially when it comes to our animals. Highly recommended! 👌

I rescued a kitten from the street who then got ill a few days after I got him. I had to take him at 2am to be seen and he was kept for 2 nights.
